known.reason: The harness, not the model: the recorder replaces the alias `c`, so the alias `d` after it is not expanded and its `declare x=1` does not run. In bash, `c d` runs `command declare x=1`, as the model says.
The harness, not the model: the recorder replaces `eval`, so `D=` does not run and `D` keeps the value the environment gave it (`a b`). In bash, `eval "D="` empties `D`, as the model says.
A CR before a LF: the model reads the text with each such CR masked as a space (`crlf`, which warns); bash gives the word its CR (oracles.md 2.6, 4).
A backslash at the very end of the input: unbash keeps it, bash drops it (docs/guide/limitations.md; test/fixtures/bash-ast-known.json; oracles.md 2.6, 5).
